title: Jobs in the Wild
hook: Harun watches the cough-syrup shelf lose to a thermos, honey, and a text from home.
counterintuition: Most teams assume a famous case should be copied. But actually the method travels only when each new setting is read on its own terms.
tryThisNow: Pick a market far from your own and write one struggling moment in it. Identify the current workaround before naming any product idea.
keyTakeaway: Jobs thinking travels across domains because people keep seeking progress in circumstances, but every new setting needs fresh evidence about pressure, substitutes, and success.

breakdown.fastRead: Harun sees a shopper leave the cough-syrup shelf with honey, lemons, and a thermos. The store lost a medicine sale, but the job did not vanish. The shopper wanted to get through a night shift without sounding sick on calls. Jobs thinking works in pharmacies, schools, freight yards, kitchens, and churches because the unit is not a category. It is progress under pressure. The danger is copying one old story. The discipline is reading each new struggle with fresh eyes.
breakdown.deepRead:
A useful idea has to travel without becoming a copy machine. The milk shake case is memorable, but the method matters more than the object. In the wild, the same lens can explain why someone chooses a study room, a cheap repair, a rideshare, a paper checklist, or a neighbor's borrowed ladder. The common structure is not the product. It is a person trying to move from one state to another under specific pressure.

At 1:12 p.m., Miko unlocks a school instrument closet while a sixth grader says she wants the dented trumpet, not the shiny one. The shiny one is better. The dented one belonged to last year's section leader, and choosing it makes the first rehearsal less lonely. The job is not instrument quality alone. It is entering a group without feeling like a visitor.

The portable move is to ask the same disciplined questions, not to expect the same answer. What struggle is active. What alternatives are real. What anxiety slows the switch. What would count as progress in this setting. The limit is local evidence. A team that imports a story from another market without field observation is not using the method. It is borrowing confidence.
breakdown.fullRead:
Jobs thinking is strongest when it crosses categories and still keeps its feet on the ground. A pharmacy choice, a school choice, a shipping choice, and a home choice can all be read through progress. That does not mean they share one hidden script. It means each contains a circumstance where a person is trying to make a situation better and has more than one possible way to do it.

This matters because category logic trains teams to look sideways at familiar rivals. A cough remedy competes with other cough remedies. A tutoring service competes with other tutoring services. A museum membership competes with other memberships. In the wild, the buyer's real field is wider and stranger. Honey and a thermos can compete with cough syrup. A YouTube explainer can compete with tutoring. A Saturday soccer schedule can compete with a museum membership. The job makes those comparisons reasonable.

Portability also demands humility. If a team hears one vivid story and pastes it across every setting, the insight becomes brittle. The new setting has its own timing, shame, workarounds, constraints, gatekeepers, and measures of success. The buyer may be trying to avoid waste, gain permission, save face, calm a child, pass a shift, or look competent in front of peers. Those differences matter.

Eleri, watching a freight dispatch board at 4:08 a.m., might learn more from the drivers' handwritten parking notes than from the official route software. The software is the category product. The notes show the job: arrive with enough certainty to sleep before the next legal driving window closes. That kind of evidence appears only when the team studies the local struggle.

The objection is that a theory that travels everywhere may explain nothing. That is fair if the theory becomes vague. The answer is specificity. A jobs claim should name the circumstance, the push away from the old way, the pull of the new option, the anxiety, the habit, and the substitute set. If it cannot do that, it has not earned the right to guide design.

So the method travels as a questioning pattern. It does not travel as a canned answer. The team can use it in any domain, but it must make the buyer's situation prove the point again each time.

examples.title: Harun watches honey beat cough syrup before shift change

planSpec.requiredBeat: he sees the job outside the aisle category

examples.scenario: Harun straightens cough syrup boxes at 10:26 p.m. in the pharmacy aisle, the floor buffer whining near the registers. A call-center supervisor reads three labels, coughs into her sleeve, then buys honey, lemons, and a steel thermos instead. Her night shift starts in thirty minutes. Harun has to decide whether the store lost to another remedy or to a plan for sounding steady on calls until sunrise.
examples.whatToDo: Treat the basket as evidence of the job. Ask what the supervisor needs the night to feel like and which non-medicine substitutes help her get there.
examples.whyItMatters: The category shelf hides rivals that matter in the moment. The thermos can be a competitor when the job is surviving a shift with a reliable voice.

examples.title: Miko hears why the dented trumpet matters

planSpec.stakes: quality measures miss entry into a group
planSpec.requiredBeat: he hears the student hire belonging, not instrument quality

examples.scenario: Miko unlocks the instrument closet at 1:12 p.m., brass cases stacked like suitcases against the cinderblock wall. "Take the clean trumpet," he says. Lani touches the dented one with a peeling blue sticker. "That was Niko's, right?" Miko nods. "He sat first chair." She keeps her hand on the old case. Miko has to decide whether to correct her toward the better instrument or hear the job: walk into rehearsal already connected to somebody.
examples.whatToDo: Ask what the dented trumpet does for Lani before judging it as inferior. Keep the social entry job visible alongside sound quality and repair cost.
examples.whyItMatters: In this setting, progress includes belonging. A technically better choice can lose if it makes the first rehearsal feel more exposed.

examples.title: Eleri studies the parking notes beside the dispatch screen

planSpec.requiredBeat: she must decide whether to trust software data or workaround evidence

examples.scenario: Eleri stands at 4:08 a.m. beside the freight dispatch board, coffee cooling in a chipped mug while drivers tape handwritten parking notes under the route screen. The software ranks on-time arrivals. The notes name restrooms, legal shoulder spots, and which loading dock lets a sleeper cab turn around. Her stylus hovers over the analytics export. She must decide whether the job is route speed or arriving with enough certainty to sleep before the driving window closes.
examples.whatToDo: Use the notes as job evidence. Interview around sleep, legal hours, turnarounds, and dock anxiety before redesigning the dispatch view.
examples.whyItMatters: The workaround reveals pressure the official metric misses. Drivers are hiring information to protect the whole shift, not only to shave minutes from a route.

examples.title: Paavo predicts coats and gets a stroller line

planSpec.stakes: visible category misses family logistics job
planSpec.requiredBeat: his coat-drive prediction fails when the queue shows another job

examples.scenario: Paavo checks the coat-drive tally at 8:33 a.m. in the church basement, predicting adult parkas will disappear first because the forecast says snow. By nine, the longest line is at the folding table with stroller blankets, mittens clipped in pairs, and bus-route cards. Parents are not only hiring warmth. They are hiring a calmer trip to daycare with both hands free. Paavo needs to choose which table gets the next volunteer before the hallway jams.
examples.whatToDo: Let the queue update the job definition. Staff the table that solves the morning transport problem, then restock around bundled trips, not only coat sizes.
examples.whyItMatters: A charity category can hide an everyday logistics job. The demand is clearer when the line shows what makes the next two hours easier.

examples.title: Zuri replays the museum membership pitch that missed Saturdays

planSpec.stakes: copying a case misses local substitutes
planSpec.requiredBeat: she sees the failed pitch ignored the family scheduling job

examples.scenario: Zuri sits under the closed museum cafe lights at 6:52 p.m., membership brochures rubber-banded beside unsold dinosaur pencils. The campaign promised unlimited wonder, but family signups fell again. Exit notes mention soccer, naps, parking, and grandparents in town for one Saturday only. The postmortem is not about wonder. Parents had hired weekends to keep the household from fraying, and the museum asked to be added without easing the plan.
examples.whatToDo: Rebuild the membership around the Saturday job. Study parking, visit length, nap timing, and grandparent use before selling unlimited access.
examples.whyItMatters: The method travels, but the answer must be local. Families were not rejecting culture, they were protecting a fragile weekend schedule.

examples.title: Gisela moves the herb bundles after watching dinner shoppers

planSpec.requiredBeat: she changes the stall after reading fresh local job evidence

examples.scenario: Gisela stacks basil at 3:05 p.m. beside the farmers market scale, rubber bands snapping against her wrist. Before, she sold herbs by variety and blamed the grocery store when bunches wilted unsold. After watching shoppers juggle fish, tomatoes, and tired children, she ties small dinner bundles with parsley, basil, and a handwritten sauce card. The stall stops competing with herb shelves and starts helping someone get Tuesday dinner across the line.
examples.whatToDo: Design from the dinner circumstance. Bundle, price, and label around the last-mile cooking job instead of the botanical category.
examples.whyItMatters: Fresh observation changes the competitive set. The rival is not only another herb seller, it is any easier way to finish dinner without waste.

questions.prompt: At 8:05 a.m., a bakery owner watches three regulars skip the croissants and buy plain coffee before the train doors close. The team is applying using jobs thinking across unlike settings without copying a story. Which next move best follows the jobs lens for this situation?
choices: Name the circumstance, the progress desired, and the substitutes already being used before changing features.
Rank customers by demographic similarity and average their requests into one roadmap item.
Ask the loudest buyer which feature would make the product seem more premium.
questions.explanation: The strongest answer starts with the pressured circumstance and the progress at stake. It treats observed behavior as evidence, then tests whether a real switch happens when that job is served better.

questions.prompt: During a 2:20 p.m. nurse handoff, a patient keeps using a pill organizer even after the app sends perfect reminders. The team is applying using jobs thinking across unlike settings without copying a story. Which interpretation should the team test before changing the product?
choices: Assume the buyer is irrational because the newer option has more features.
Treat the visible workaround as evidence of a struggling moment, then ask what it helps the buyer avoid or achieve.
Lower the price first, then look for explanations after volume changes.
questions.explanation: The strongest answer starts with the pressured circumstance and the progress at stake. It treats observed behavior as evidence, then tests whether a real switch happens when that job is served better.

choices: Ask which color, size, and interface label each segment prefers.

questions.prompt: On a rainy Saturday at 11:10 a.m., a hardware clerk notices renters buying tape, towels, and a cheap fan together. The team is applying using jobs thinking across unlike settings without copying a story. Which sign matters most for judging the real competitor?
choices: The substitute set the buyer compares in the moment, including awkward fixes outside the formal category.
The products displayed closest on the shelf, because they share the same category label.
The competitor with the highest advertising spend in the annual report.

questions.prompt: At 9:48 p.m., a founder reads cancellation notes that praise the product but mention setup dread in every third line. The team is applying using jobs thinking across unlike settings without copying a story. Which response avoids mistaking polite feedback for causal evidence?
choices: Treat every compliment as proof that the positioning is already clear.
Separate praise from switching evidence and look for anxiety, habit, push, and pull in the actual story.
Rewrite the website copy around the most flattering quote.
questions.explanation: The strongest answer starts with the pressured circumstance and the progress at stake. It treats observed behavior as evidence, then tests whether a real switch happens when that job is served better.

questions.prompt: Before a 7:30 a.m. board review, a transit planner compares riders who buy weekly passes with riders who pay one fare at a time. The team is applying using jobs thinking across unlike settings without copying a story. Which data cut would make the choice pattern less blurry?
choices: Blend all buyers into one persona so the team has a cleaner deck.
Focus only on lifetime value and ignore the purchase moment.
Split behavior by occasion and pressure, then compare what each group is trying to get done.
questions.explanation: The strongest answer starts with the pressured circumstance and the progress at stake. It treats observed behavior as evidence, then tests whether a real switch happens when that job is served better.

questions.prompt: At 4:12 p.m., a dentist sees a teenager use whitening strips carefully but abandon the prescribed night guard. The team is applying using jobs thinking across unlike settings without copying a story. Which design move respects the social and emotional pressure in the moment?
choices: Reduce the friction that makes the buyer feel exposed, guilty, rushed, or incompetent in that setting.
Add a technically superior feature even if it makes the buyer feel more watched.
Tell users they should care more about the functional benefit.
questions.explanation: The strongest answer starts with the pressured circumstance and the progress at stake. It treats observed behavior as evidence, then tests whether a real switch happens when that job is served better.

questions.prompt: While closing a library desk at 5:55 p.m., a clerk watches students book tiny rooms even when large tables are empty. The team is applying using jobs thinking across unlike settings without copying a story. Which observation most clearly points to a job rather than a category preference?
choices: The buyer says the category is interesting during a survey.
The buyer uses the option when a specific situation appears, even when other category choices are available.
The buyer recognizes the logo without remembering the purchase.
questions.explanation: The strongest answer starts with the pressured circumstance and the progress at stake. It treats observed behavior as evidence, then tests whether a real switch happens when that job is served better.

questions.prompt: At 10:03 a.m., a farm co-op manager hears growers ask for faster invoices while carrying handwritten notebooks. The team is applying using jobs thinking across unlike settings without copying a story. Which experiment would test whether the stated request matches the real hire?
choices: Ask the sales team to vote on the most elegant feature name.
Copy the category leader and wait for the market to notice.
Stage a small test around the moment of struggle and watch whether the buyer switches without being coached.
questions.explanation: The strongest answer starts with the pressured circumstance and the progress at stake. It treats observed behavior as evidence, then tests whether a real switch happens when that job is served better.

reviewCards.front: A customer praises the product but keeps using a clumsy workaround. What should you retrieve first?
reviewCards.back: Retrieve the situation before the quote. Ask when the workaround appears, what progress it protects, and which anxiety keeps the customer from switching cleanly.

reviewCards.front: You see one product used in two different moments. What move keeps the analysis sharp?
reviewCards.back: Separate the moments. A shared product name can hide different jobs, different substitutes, and different standards for what good means.

reviewCards.front: A roadmap debate turns into feature ranking. How do you bring back portable job diagnosis?
reviewCards.back: Put the buyer's struggling moment on the table, name the progress being hired, and judge each feature by whether it helps that movement happen.

reviewCards.front: A team has a beautiful story from one buyer. What question prevents overreach?
reviewCards.back: Ask which evidence repeats across similar circumstances and which details are local. A job story earns power through repeated hires, not through one vivid quote.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: Practice reading demand from the situation before judging the product. The skill is to name the progress a person is trying to make, list the substitutes already in play, and test whether your offer helps that progress better than the current workaround.

ifThenPlans.plan: If a meeting starts ranking feature ideas, then write the buyer's exact moment of struggle at the top of the notes and force every option to answer how it improves portable job diagnosis.
If you abandon a tool that looked sensible, then pause for one minute and name what the old habit protected before you replace it with another polished option.
If a repeated purchase feels oddly satisfying or oddly disappointing, then write the time, place, substitute, and desired progress before deciding what to buy next.
If someone asks for a surface fix, then ask what situation made the request urgent and what would feel better after the fix works.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Within the next day, catch one choice while it is happening. Write the clock time, the place, the old workaround, the anxiety around switching, and one sentence naming the progress you are hiring the option to deliver.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once this week, interview one person about a recent switch. Do not start with features. Reconstruct the moment, the push away from the old way, the pull of the new way, and the substitute they almost kept.

memorableLines.text: Honey and a thermos can compete with cough syrup.
memorableLines.why: It makes the wider competitive set concrete with an unexpected image.

memorableLines.why: It captures the central paradox in one memorable sentence.
